rubric.evidence: Every normative claim traces to a fetched primary source: CSS Overflow 3 §3/§3.1 (scrollable/non-scrollable values, single-axis rule, clip definition — quoted verbatim 2026-07-29), CSS Position 3 §3.4 (per-axis sticky resolution, quoted verbatim), WPT assertions (quoted), runtime_enabled_features.json5, and chromium-review CL states (8127263 verified NEW at fetch time).

Slug and folder derive from the exact listing name 'Single-axis scroll containers' in the milestone=153 listing ('Enabled by default' group, verified 2026-07-29). The stale detail-record status ('Proposed') and the unmerged enable-by-default CL are disclosed in the ship-status warn-block rather than smoothed over; the listing is treated as authoritative per invariant #2.

reference-contract.json claims implementation-sufficient: 4 inventory items (combination grammar, container-type definitions, sticky resolution algorithm, disabled-axis API behavior) × 9 dimensions, one sourced not-applicable (definitions have no error surface). Validated by validate-artifacts + test-reference-contract.

Leads with the developer-relevant framing (why clip not hidden), a combination-outcome table, and a resolution walk-through; the ambiguous feature name is pinned to concrete sources (overflow-side and sticky-side) in the lede and at-a-glance.

Canonical split-axis data-grid pattern (CSS + outcome table), axis-lock snippet, and a JS scroll-API snippet on the child page. Examples are source-derived but not executed against a Chrome 153 build (no local binary with the flag).

No BCD key records this behavior — the page says so explicitly and explains why BCD multiple_keywords (Chrome 68) must NOT be read as support for it; the compat table is labelled interim and compiled from primary sources with explicit no-signal rows.

All citations are direct hyperlinks (zero plain-text labels); external links fetched live during research (spec anchors, PR/issue states, CL states, WPT files, BCD JSON, webstatus, vendor position issues).

Landmark main, sequential headings, table th scoping, AA-safe palette via public/styles.css variables; the page itself documents the clip-axis accessibility hazard (content unreachable by scrolling). Guidance applied from the accessibility guide (structure/landmarks).

css-layout guidance applied: tables in .table-wrap with overflow-wrap:anywhere cells, pre blocks scroll internally, h1/lede overflow-wrap:anywhere. Screenshots read at 390px and 1280px for all three routes (see progress notes).

CPS route /v153/single-axis-scroll-containers/ returned 404 at check time (2026-07-29), so per the Case B fallback rule no iframe is embedded; the page links the route textually and states the 404 plainly.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive data tables reference documentation layout
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Lean on intrinsic sizing and the browser layout engine; avoid hardcoded dimensions; keep overflow contained.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Tables render inside .table-wrap{overflow-x:auto} with overflow-wrap:anywhere on cells and no fixed pixel widths; pre blocks scroll internally; h1/lede use overflow-wrap:anywhere for the long feature name.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive data tables reference documentation layout
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Place content within landmarks, keep heading order sequential, scope table headers.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Single main landmark; h1→h2 sequential; doc-tables use th scope=row/col; color relies on the AA-checked public/styles.css palette.
